what: The score is the fixed-position geometric insertion increase minus the candidate's distance from the depot. It is a generalized cheapest-insertion criterion with a depot-distance credit and costs O(1) time and memory per call.
why: Pure cheapest insertion can repeatedly select easy near-depot customers and leave remote customers for later routes, creating additional long depot legs. Since each route is seeded by its farthest remaining customer, the depot-distance credit encourages adding other remote customers when they can be inserted into that route at reasonable cost, while the insertion term still discourages geographically incompatible choices. This also emphasizes route membership rather than exact order, which is appropriate when intra-route 2-opt follows construction. The rule is deliberately simple and parameter-free, but it does not explicitly model demand packing, future feasible insertions, or the spatial distribution of other unassigned customers, so its benefit must be validated on held-out instances.
